entries.algorithm_variant: scipy.signal.savgol_filter(window_length=5, polyorder=2, mode='interp', delta=1.0), applied along the variable axis. SciPy solves a least-squares system per output position; our kernel builds one convolution matrix from the pseudo-inverse of the window's Vandermonde matrix. Same filter, independent code paths - scipy.signal is never called by the kernel.
entries.citation: Generated by tests/fixtures/generate_reference_values.py against SciPy 1.18.1. Not a literature value: an open implementation pinned by version, reproducible by anyone.
entries.notes: Computed on the first 5 samples and first 8 variables of the dataset. The transform is independent per row or per column, so the block tests it completely. Derivatives are per variable index (delta=1), not per axis unit.

entries.algorithm_variant: scipy.signal.savgol_filter(window_length=5, polyorder=2, mode='interp', delta=1.0), applied along the variable axis. SciPy solves a least-squares system per output position; our kernel builds one convolution matrix from the pseudo-inverse of the window's Vandermonde matrix. Same filter, independent code paths - scipy.signal is never called by the kernel.

Window 5, polyorder 2, edge mode **interp**: with a half-window of 2, the first and last 2 of the 8 columns are evaluated off the centre of the end window rather than padded, so this block tests the edge convention and not only the interior. Derivatives are per variable index (delta=1), not per axis unit.

entries.citation: Mevik, B.-H., Wehrens, R. and Liland, K. H., 'Introduction to the pls Package', vignette for R package pls, https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pls/vignettes/pls-manual.html (retrieved 2026-08-22). Underlying data: Kalivas, J. H. (1997), 'Two data sets of near infrared spectra', Chemometrics and Intelligent Laboratory Systems 37, 255-259.
entries.notes: The vignette's 'CV' row, printed to four significant figures. Key '0' is the intercept-only model. R pls computes MSEP as SSE/nobj (mvrVal.R), so its divisor is n and the values are directly comparable with our RMSECV with no definitional correction. The vignette's 'adjCV' row is a bias-corrected estimate we do not report and is deliberately not recorded here. Do not read this curve against gasoline.pls.rmsecv_curve.sklearn as if the two were the same experiment: that one is 5-fold over all 60 samples, this one is LOO over the first 50. They agree closely from about five components (0.2398 here against 0.2396 there) and differ at two, where the estimate is far more sensitive to the split.

SNV and MSC are checked against their defining identities instead - an SNV row has mean 0 and standard deviation 1 by construction, and MSC of the reference spectrum returns the reference. Those are exact properties rather than a second opinion, so this stays a gap. chemotools, evaluated in #13, would fill it.

entries.notes: Neither SciPy nor scikit-learn implements baseline correction, and no other implementation is installed here. The three methods are checked against their defining properties instead - a rubberband baseline lies on the lower convex hull and never above the spectrum, a polynomial baseline of degree d removes a degree-d polynomial exactly, and AsLS reaches a fixed point of its own reweighting. Those are exact properties rather than a second opinion, so this stays a gap. `pybaselines` is the obvious reference and adding it is a dependency decision, not a kernel one.
